content: The American Diabetes Association (ADA) recognizes the importance of addressing diabetes distress and has identified several effective interventions. Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) has been shown to significantly alleviate diabetes-related emotional distress while also contributing to improved glycemic control, as evidenced by better A1C levels. Similarly, mindfulness-based therapy has proven effective in reducing the psychological burden associated with diabetes management. Additionally, digital tools, including smartphone applications, have emerged as practical and accessible platforms for delivering CBT and other therapeutic approaches, further aiding in the reduction of diabetes distress.
